collected_dynamic_variables.pain_points: Missing about 9 calls weekly; roughly half would’ve booked and the rest move on to someone else, Calls go to voicemail; inconsistent callback/follow-up (if I remember), Missed calls happen mostly daytime while on jobs; some after-hours too, Callers often go to the next plumber; back-and-forth to connect is a hassle

transcript:
User: Yeah, what.
Agent: Yeah, I am — I’m Linda, an AI assistant on Jay’s team at Dialux, and I help with the intro and getting you set up for a live walkthrough. What made you call today?
User: Didn't call. You called me. What's this about?
Agent: Got it—sorry about the surprise. We help businesses stop losing revenue from missed calls when you’re busy or no one can pick up; are you the owner or the person who handles the phones?
User: I'm the owner. Handle most things. What you offering?
Agent: Got it. We help you capture and convert missed calls—when you can’t answer, we respond right away, qualify the job, and get it booked instead of losing it. What’s been happening with missed calls on your end lately?
User: Miss about 9 calls weekly.
Agent: Got it—when those 9 calls go unanswered, what usually happens next?
User: Half maybe would've booked, rest move on.
Agent: Yeah, that’s exactly the revenue-leak we see—if they can’t reach you, they just call the next company. What kind of business are you in?
User: Plumbing. Szymanski & Sons. Fix leaks, pipes.
Agent: Got it—plumbing, Szymanski & Sons. When calls come in and you’re on a job, where do they go right now—voicemail, call-back list, or someone else picks up?
User: Voicemail mostly. Sometimes I call back if I remember.
Agent: Makes sense—so a lot of those leads are sitting in voicemail, and the follow-up’s hit-or-miss. Are most of those missed calls during the day while you’re on jobs, or after-hours?
User: Daytime. Busy with jobs mostly. Some after-hours too.
Agent: Got it—daytime on jobs, and a few after-hours too. When someone hits voicemail, do you lose them mostly because they call the next plumber, or because the back-and-forth takes too long?
User: Yeah, mostly they call the next one. Back-and-forth also a hassle sometimes.
Agent: Yeah, I hear you—plumbing customers don’t wait around. If you had something that answered those calls and booked the job while you’re on-site, would you want to see how it works?
User: Sure, sure. How's that work? Time is money, spare me the fluff.
Agent: Totally—no fluff: we route your missed calls to our 24/7 answering line that sounds human, grabs the address/issue, and either books the job or warm-transfers to you if it’s urgent. Mind if I do a 30‑second back-of-napkin on what those 9 missed calls a week are costing you?
User: Fine, but keep it brief. I ain't got all day.
Agent: Got it—I’ll keep it tight. What’s your average job value, roughly: $300, $600, $1,000?
User: $380 average. That's what we charge.
Agent: Got it—so if you miss ~9 calls a week and even half would’ve booked at $380, that’s about **$7,400/month** slipping away. It’s a 20‑minute walkthrough with Jay so you can see exactly how it’d plug that gap—what’s better for you, later today or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow works. Keep it short. When exactly?
Agent: Got it—we’ll keep it to 20 minutes. Before I lock a time, what’s your first name?
User: Gene. Make it quick, 20 minutes max. Enough with questions, just finish up.
Agent: Got it, Gene—and yep, 20 minutes max. Is the number you’re calling from the best number to text the confirmation to?
User: Sure, sure. Text it to +18165550022.
Agent: Got it—thank you. And which time zone are you in: Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?
User: Central. Kansas City, Missouri. Anything else?
Agent: Central—perfect. Tomorrow (Thu 8/27) I can do **11:30 AM** or **12:15 PM** Central; which one works?
User: Fine, fine. Book the thing for 11:30 AM.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Thanks, Gene—you’re all set for **tomorrow at 11:30 AM Central** with Jay. You’ll receive an SMS text with the confirmation details so you can add it to your calendar or reschedule if you need to.  

Is there anything else I can help you with?
User: Unbelievable. Takes forever. Confirm quick, I got pipes to fix.
Agent: Totally hear you, Gene. You’re booked for tomorrow at 11:30 AM Central, and the SMS confirmation is on its way. Really glad you took the time—Jay’s looking forward to it. Have a great rest of your day. Bye!
